Very Important Publication
An Allene Approach to Tetrahydrofuran-Fused Bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-
2-enes
Shihua Song, a Chunling Fu, a Xin Huang, a,* and Shengming Ma a,*
a Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310027,
Zhejiang, People’s Republic of China
Fax: (+ 86)21-6260-9305; e-mail: xinhuangzju@zju.edu.cn; masm@sioc.ac.cn
Received: November 2, 2017; Revised: December 4, 2017; Published online: December 27, 2017
Supporting information for this article is available on the WWW under https://doi.org/10.1002/adsc.201701407
Abstract: An efficient access to tetrahydrofuran-
fused bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-2-enes via palladium-cata-
lyzed cyclization of oxygen-tethered 2,7-alkadiy-
nylic carbonates with 2-(buta-2,3-dienyl)malononi-
trile has been developed. Perfect chiral induction
was observed when a substituent was introduced to
the propargylic position affording the optically
active polycyclic products of both enantiomers.
Control experiments showed that the oxygen tether
of 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonates and the two cyano
groups in allene are indispensible for this trans-
formation.
Keywords: palladium; polycycle; allene; 2,7-alka-
diynylic carbonates
During the last 10 to 15 years much attention has been
paid to transition metal-catalyzed cyclization reactions
of different types of allenes.
[1, 2] In this area, we have
studied the cyclization of allenes bearing a nucleo-
philic functionality in the presence of 2,7-alkadiynyl
carbonates affording tricyclic products A,
[3a] B,[3b] or
C.[4] Interestingly when 2-(buta-2,3-dienyl)malononi-
trile was used instead of allenoic acids, allenyl amides,
or allenyl malonate or bis(phenylsulfonyl)methane,
tetrahydrofuran-fused bicycle[2.2.2]oct-2-enes 3 was
formed unexpectedly. The core structure D, a bicy-
clo[2.2.2]oct-2-ene fused with a tetrahydrofuran ring,
is also a structural element of Tokinolide B and
Diligustilide, which have been isolated from the
extracts of rhizome of L. porter. They show significant
inhibitory effects against inflammation
[5a] and human
cancer cells. [5b] In addition, a more complex and
potential chemical, chanxiongnolide B, [5c] was also
isolated. From a pharmacological point of view, an
efficient access to such bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-2-ene fused
with a tetrahydrofuran ring D may lead to the
discovery of new lead compounds. However, the
existing synthesis of such bridged core structure D is
still very limited.
[6] In this paper, we wish to report this
efficient palladium-catalyzed entry to tetrahydrofur-
an-fused bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-2-enes 3 from the readily
available oxygen-tethered 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonates
with 2-(buta-2,3-dienyl)malononitrile (Scheme 1).
Initially, when 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonate ( 1a ) was
subjected to react with 2-(buta-2,3-dienyl)malononi-
trile ( 2a ) under the catalysis of Pd(OAc)
2/Gorlos-
Phos · HBF4
[7a] using K2CO3 as the base at 50 8C for 7 h
in CH 3CN, quite unexpectedly, a new product ( 3a )
containing a bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-2-ene fused with a
tetrahydrofuran ring was formed (Table 1, entry 3). Its
structure was established by X-ray diffraction analysis
(Figure 1).
[8]
Due to the above-mentioned importance of such a
core structure D in Scheme 1, we set out to optimize
the reaction conditions. Initially, various phosphorus
ligands and palladium resources were examined.
When submitting Pd(OAc)
2 as catalyst with LB-
Phos · HBF4
[7b] or Zheda-Phos · HBF 4
[7c] as ligand, the
reaction failed (Table 1, entries 1 and 2). By using
Gorlos-Phos · HBF
4, the bridged polycycle 3a was
formed in a yield of 12% in addition to 4% of 4a [3]
and 1% of 5a [4] with recovery of 1a in 57% yield
Figure 1. The ORTEP Representation of 3a .

(Table 1, entry 3). With DBA (dibenzylideneacetone)
as a ligand very limited improvement was observed
(Table 1, entry 4). Interestingly, PPh
3 gave a moderate
yield of 3a of 50%, however, more 4a and 5a were
produced too (Table 1, entry 5). Pd(PPh 3)4 showed a
slightly lower efficiency but a better selectivity
(Table 1, entry 6). Pd(PPh 3)2Cl2 gave a better yield of
51% for 3a and the reaction selectivity was improved
further (Table 1, entry 7). Some other experimental
parameters were also screened and found that the
molar ratio of reactants has a great influence on the
reaction: 57% yield of 3a and 6% of 4a were observed
with a molar ratio of 1a /2a being 1/2 (Table 1,
entry 8). With K
3PO4 as a base, the formation of 4a
was surpressed to 2% with 61% of 3a being formed
(Table 1, entry 10). Thus, 2a (2.0 equiv), Pd(PPh 3)2Cl2
(5 mol%), K 3PO4 (1.0 equiv) in CH 3CN at 50 8C have
been defined as the standard reaction conditions for
further study.
With the optimized conditions in hand, the sub-
strate scope of the reaction was examined. The
reaction proceeded well on a gram-scale (Table 2,
entry 3). The electronic effect of the Ar group has a
very limited impact on the efficiency of the trans-
formation: A carbon-halogen bond on the benzene
ring is also tolerated (Table 2, entries 5 and 6), which
makes it possible for further functionalization; thienyl
is also compatible (Table 2, entry 7). R
1 may be two
alkyl groups or a cyclic alkyl group (Table 2, en-
tries 9 ~ 11).
When non-symmetric 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonate
1k was reacted with 2-(buta-2,3-dien-1-yl)malononi-
trile, ( Z)-3k and ( E)-3k were produced in 51% yield
with a Z/E ratio of 2.3:1. The configurations of ( Z)-3k
and (E)-3k were tentatively assigned by NOE analysis
(see eq. 1).

Furthermore, it is exciting to observe that the
reactions of racemic compounds 1l and 1m afforded
3l and 3m as one diastereomer exclusively, respec-
tively. Thus, the reactions of optically active ( R)-1l
and its enantiomer ( S)-1l were tried and the enan-
tiomers, (1 R,3R,7S)-3l and (1 S,3S,7R)-3l , were
formed, exclusively, demonstrating an interesting
highly efficient chiral induction to control all the
remaining absolute configurations (Scheme 2). Their
absolute configurations were established by X-ray
diffraction analysis.
[9]
To our surprise, the cascade reaction towards 3
failed when 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonate 1 was tethered
with CH 2 or NTs, indicating a unique role of the
oxygen atom. Unfortunately, the reaction of sulfur-
tethered 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonate also did not afford
the expected tricyclic product either, which may be
caused by the poison of the palladium catalyst by the
sulfur atom. In addition, when one CN group in 2a
was replaced with a methoxycarbonyl group ( 2b ), no
bridged polycyclic product was formed, indicting the

On the basis of above results, a plausible mecha-
nism was tentatively proposed as shown in Scheme 4
by taking the reaction of 1a with 2a as the example.
Oxidative addition of 1a with the catalytically active
species Pd(0) would give the allenylpalladium inter-
mediate IN-1,
[10,1l] which undergoes intramolecular
insertion of the triple bond to generate the alkenylpal-
ladium species IN-2.
[11] The species IN-2 undergoes
highly regioselective intermolecular carbopalladation
of the internal C =C bond of the allene moiety in 2a to
generate a new stereodefined alkenylpalladium inter-
mediate IN-3 due to the side-on coordination of C /C17N
with palladium ( Path a ).
[12] Then intramolecular
carbopalladation of allene would form a new allylpal-
ladium intermediate IN-4 or IN-4’. In presence of a
base, the key intermediate IN-4 or IN-4’could under-
go intramolecular nucleophilic attack forming bridged
tricyclic product 3a and regenerating the catalytically
active Pd(0). The intermediate IN-2 may also undergo
intermolecular carbopalladation of the terminal C =C
bond of the allene moiety in 2a to generate a
stereodefined alkenylpalladium intermediate IN-5
with palladium coordinated with C /C17N in side-on
mode ( Path b ).
[3b] Then intramolecular carbopallada-
tion of allene and intramolecular nucleophilic attack
would form tricyclic intermediate IN-7 and regenerate
the catalytically active Pd(0). After aromatization, the
side-product 4a was delivered. Compared with path b,
the coordination of the two CN groups with Pd may
have determined the regioselectivity of the insertion
reaction forming intermediate IN-3.
In summary, we have developed a highly efficient
approach to tetrahydrofuran-fused bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-2-
enes from the readily available oxygen-tethered 2,7-
alkadiynylic carbonates and 2-(buta-2,3-dien-1-yl)ma-
lononitrile under the catalysis of palladium. This
transformation features mild conditions and efficiency
to such a complicated skeleton. Optically active
bridged products also can be yielded with perfect
chiral induction. Control experiments show that the
oxygen tether of 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonates and the
two cyano groups of allenes are critical for this
transformation although the role of these function-
alities is not clear to us. The further utilization of the
transformation and study on the role of each reactant
are going on in our research group.
Experimental Section
General Experimental Methods
Pd(PPh3)2Cl2 was purchased from Energy Chemical. K 3PO4
was purchased from Shanghai Titan Scientific Co., Ltd.
CH3CN used was dried over CaH 2 under reflux conditions
and distilled just before use. The synthesis of starting
material 2,7-alkadiynylic carbonates 1a –1c , 1e, 1h –1i , and
1l –1n were prepared according to the literature proce-
dures.[4] The boiling range of the petroleum ether was 30–
60 8C unless noted otherwise. Other commercially available
chemicals were purchased and used without additional
purification unless noted otherwise. All
1H NMR experi-
ments were measured with tetramethylsilane (0 ppm) or the
signal of CHCl 3 (7.26 ppm) in CDCl 3 as the internal
reference; 13C NMR experiments were measured in relative
to the signal of CDCl 3 (77.0 ppm); 19F NMR experiments
were measured in relative to the signal of CFCl 3 (0 ppm) in
CDCl3. Infrared spectra were recorded from the film of pure
samples on sodium chloride plates for liquid. Mass and
HRMS spectra were carried out in EI mode. Elemental
analyses were carried out by Elementar V ario MICRO cube.
Thin layer chromatography was performed on pre-coated
glassback plates and visualized with UV light at 254 nm.
Flash column chromatography was performed on silica gel.
